attrs.evidence: probe_ownfailopen_9d3_repro.mjs, 0/3 confined against World 0.10.0 and 3/3 against 0.11.0 with named refusals. A witness carrying a method defeated both mechanisms and came back by reference; a Map witness passed structuredClone while Object.freeze left its ENTRIES writable — and since JSON.stringify(Map) is '{}', Map([['e',1]]) and Map([['e',999]]) were indistinguishable to warrant identity, so the ownership domain and the identity domain disagreed about what a value is; and spec.inputs took the whole registration-alias species back, with B re-deriving on a caller-mutated input mid-pass.
attrs.statement: An ownership boundary that cannot own an object must REFUSE the object, never return the caller's reference. v0.10.0 ended in `catch { return v }`, so anything neither canonicalBytes nor structuredClone could handle was handed straight back with the authority the layer existed to take. Ownership now goes through canonicalBytes alone and throws <field>-not-canonical on failure, for spec.inputs, warrant.value and warrant.witness alike. A witness may be semantically OPAQUE without being representationally ARBITRARY: if it participates in warrant_id it needs a canonical representation. Should tagged encodings for Map/Set/Date ever be required, one encoding must serve ownership, equality, warrant_id and replay together.
